court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Ashish Ashok Naik And Anr vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ashish Ashok Naik and another (original accused)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra and another

facts_of_case: Parties have arrived at amicable settlement. Parties have worked out consent terms.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding offences under Section 320 of the Code.
legal_principles.held: The Supreme Court has made following observations: The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
Kulwinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2007) 4 CTC 769
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in settling matrimonial disputes
